anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: «Θαρσεῖτε … ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον» matches John 16:33 (θαρσεῖτε, ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον); φησίν is Christ.
«Ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος» is marked as a quotation in the edition: LXX Malachi 3:20 (ἀνατελεῖ … ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης), English Malachi 4:2; ἀνέτειλεν echoes ἀνατελεῖ. LXX numbering converted.

«καίουσι λύχνον καὶ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τιθέασιν … ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν» follows Matthew 5:15 (οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν); Hesychius breaks the verse with his own glosses on 'basket' (the Law) and 'lamp' (the Word). Cited once at the first part of the quotation.

choices.term: φαιδρότερα δὲ τὰ σύμπαντα ἑωσφόρου ἀνατέλλοντος
choices.english: the whole universe is brighter still when the morning star rises
choices.why: τὰ σύμπαντα ('all things together') is the subject of the comparative, not the sky; ἑωσφόρος is the morning star.
rejected: it is even brighter with the rising of the dawn-bringer

choices.english: is lit up not so much by the stars
choices.why: ἄστροις is the instrument of καταυγάζεται ('is lit up by'), set against ἀγάλλεται.
rejected: does not gleam so much for the stars

choices.why: Middle of ἀποφέρω, 'carry off (as a prize), win'; the hearers receive the gifts, they do not offer them. The same verb in the future (ἀποισόμεθα) is 'shall win'.
δᾳδουχία is a carrying of torches, the lights of the paschal night.

choices.term: καὶ τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοίξαντος
choices.english: and the emblems of the cross that opened the doors of heaven to us
choices.why: The second dative is a further object of προσκυνείτω, which takes the dative, and τοῦ ἀνοίξαντος agrees with σταυροῦ, so no verb is supplied.
rejected: which has opened the doors of heaven to us (said of the wood)

choices.why: λυχνία is the stand, λύχνος the lamp; Hesychius keeps them apart (the lamp is the Word).

edition.locus: U 01 opening (superscription and §§1-2 to τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης)

lemmas.gloss: let us keep as a festival

pass_a_gloss: [Heading] Of the blessed Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, into the holy Pascha. [The Latin catalogue line above it is an editor's heading and is not glossed.] Bright is the heaven, being lit up by the choral dance of the stars, and brighter are all things together when the dawn-bringer is rising; but the present state of the night is shone upon not so much by stars as now it exults, our God and Savior having conquered. 'Take heart,' for, he says, 'I have conquered the world.' And God having conquered the unseen enemy, fittingly we ourselves also shall carry off the victory against demons. Let us stay, therefore, by the saving cross, so that we may carry off the first first-fruits of the gifts of Jesus. This holy night let us keep festival with holy torch processions, raising a God-filled song and singing out a heavenly hymn. 'The sun of righteousness', the Lord of us Jesus Christ, both lit up the present day for the circle of the inhabited world, rose up through cross, saved through the faithful. Let no one, then, disbelieve the symbols of the cross, but let him bow in worship to the blessed and thrice-blessed wood of the cross, and to the symbols of the cross which opened doors of heaven for us. No longer 'they kindle a lamp and under the measure-basket they set it', and basket I call the Law, 'but upon the lampstand', and lamp the Word; and under the Law was the Word and was hidden from the faithless, as under the basket; but when he came upon cross and upon the lampstand was set, then to the of the inhabited world [continues in u01-rem-early: circle he shone upon].
pass_b_english: Of the blessed Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, on the Holy Pascha.

The sky is bright, lit up by the dance of the stars, and the whole universe is brighter still when the morning star rises. Yet this present night is lit up not so much by the stars as it now exults because our God and Savior has conquered. For 'Take courage,' he says, 'I have overcome the world' (John 16:33). And since God has conquered the invisible enemy, we too shall rightly win the victory over the demons. Let us, then, stay beside the saving cross, so that we may win the first fruits of the gifts of Jesus. Let us keep this holy night as a festival with holy torchlight, raising a song inspired by God and singing out a heavenly hymn. 'The sun of righteousness' (Malachi 4:2), our Lord Jesus Christ, has lit up this present day for the whole circle of the world; he rose through the cross; he saved the faithful.

Let no one, then, distrust the emblems of the cross; rather, let him worship the blessed and thrice-blessed wood of the cross, and the emblems of the cross that opened the doors of heaven to us. No longer do 'they light a lamp and put it under the basket' (Matthew 5:15), and by the basket I mean the Law, 'but on the lampstand', and by the lamp I mean the Word. For the Word was under the Law and was hidden from unbelievers, as under the basket; but when he came to the cross and was set on the lampstand, then across the world's…
source_text:
Homilia i in sanctum pascha (homilia 3) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 492)
Τοῦ μακαρίου Ἡσυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πάσχα
1 Φαιδρὸς ὁ οὐρανὸς τῇ τῶν ἄστρων χορείᾳ καταλαμπόμε νος, φαιδρότερα δὲ
τὰ σύμπαντα ἑωσφόρου ἀνατέλλοντος, ἀλλ' ἡ παροῦσα τῆς νυκτὸς κατάστασις οὐ
τοσοῦτον ἄστροις καταυ γάζεται ὁπόσον νῦν ἀγάλλεται τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν
νε νικηκότος· «Θαρσεῖτε» γάρ, φησίν, «ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κό σμον»· θεοῦ δὲ
νικήσαντος τὸν ἀόρατον πολέμιον, εἰκότως καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν κατὰ δαιμόνων νίκην
ἀποισόμεθα. Παραμείνωμεν τοί νυν τῷ σωτηριώδει σταυρῷ, ἵνα τὰς πρώτας ἀπαρχὰς
τῶν Ἰησοῦ δώρων ἀπενεγκώμεθα. Τὴν ἱερὰν ταύτην νύκτα δᾳ δουχίαις ἱεραῖς
πανηγυρίσωμεν, μέλος ἔνθεον ἐγείροντες καὶ ὕ μνον οὐράνιον ἐξᾴδοντες. «Ὁ τῆς
δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος», ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, καὶ τὴν παροῦσαν ἡμέραν τῷ
κύκλῳ τῆς οἰκουμένης κατεφώτισεν, διὰ σταυροῦ ἀνέτειλεν, τοὺς πιστοὺς διέσωσεν.
2 Μή τις τοίνυν ἀπιστείτω τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις, ἀλλὰ τὸ μακάριον
καὶ τρισμακάριον ξύλον τοῦ σταυροῦ προσκυνείτω, καὶ τοῖς τοῦ σταυροῦ συμβόλοις
τοῦ θύρας οὐρανοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνοί ξαντος. Οὐκέτι «καίουσι λύχνον καὶ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον
τιθέασιν», μόδιον δέ φημι τὸν Νόμον, «ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν», λύχνον δὲ τὸν Λόγον·
ὑπὸ τὸν Νόμον δὲ ἐτύγχανεν καὶ ἐκρύπτετο τοῖς ἀπίστοις ὁ Λόγος ὡς ὑπὸ τὸν
μόδιον· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν ἐπὶ σταυροῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν ἐτέθη, τότε τῷ τῆς οἰκουμένης
source_normalizations: Line-break splits joined (καταλαμπόμε νος, καταυ γάζεται, νε νικηκότος, κό σμον, τοί νυν, δᾳ δουχίαις, ὕ μνον, ἀνοί ξαντος); no letters added.
The Latin catalogue line 'Homilia i in sanctum pascha (homilia 3) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 492)' is an editor's heading and is not translated; the section numbers 1 and 2 are kept as paragraph breaks.

review_notes: The English is the reviewer's retranslation from rv0.json; it replaces the earlier machine draft, whose wording, gloss and checks no longer apply (backup in outputs/waveA-20261023/hesychius-homilia-i-pascha/backup-cleanup/).

Row begins at the start of the homily (the Greek superscription is translated as the first paragraph) and closes mid-sentence ('then across the world's…'), joined by '…whole circle he shone out.' at the start of u01-rem-early.

Every clause checked against the Greek: the bright sky and the morning star, the night exulting in God's victory, the call to stay by the cross and keep the night with torchlight and song, the sun of righteousness, the worship of the wood and emblems of the cross, and the lamp and lampstand read as the Law and the Word.
Scripture checked: John 16:33, Malachi 4:2 (LXX Malachi 3:20, numbering converted), Matthew 5:15.
